sentences.text: Two more parts of Rule eight.
Your action must get you past at a safe distance, and you keep checking that it’s working until the other vessel is finally past and clear.
If you need more time to figure things out, slow down, stop, or back down.
Slowing down is always on the menu, and it buys you time.
Rule eight also defines a phrase you’ll meet again and again: not to impede.
A vessel required not to impede another must act early, leaving plenty of room.
And that duty doesn’t disappear just because the boats get close and a risk of collision develops.
Next time, we’ll head into narrow channels and the big-ship highways called traffic separation schemes, where small boats like ours have special duties.
